newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end sharply down as JGBs plummet.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end sharply down as JGBs plummet.

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen futures on TIFFE ended Friday's day session sharply down.
Euroyen futures followed in the footsteps of Japanese government bonds all day, a city bank trader said.
The June began falling in the early morning as JGBs were sold due to a rumour that a foreign news agency was carrying an article suggesting a possible credit tightening by the Bank of Japan.
A BOJ official said he was unaware of the rumour and therefore could not comment.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, payments of one-year fixed interest rates were seen again this morning, a trader for another city bank said.
"Hedge sales of such payments are finding their way into the Euroyen futures (market)," the trader said.
Unless such payments of fixed interest rates in the IRS market come to an end, Euroyen futures are likely to be kept under downward pressure, the trader added.
Turnover for the June was 143,137 contracts.
Earlier, some traders had said they felt 99.09 would be a key support for the June, but the key Euroyen futures contract fell as low as 99.05 during the day. The day's high was 99.16.
A trust bank trader said 99.04, which is where the fifty day moving average lies, may lend some support to the June.
The BOJ refrained from conducting its regular 0020 GMT money market operation on Friday, maintaining its neutral money market stance.
The overnight call rate was traded at 0.47 percent in the afternoon, having been traded at around 0.45 percent in the morning, a trader for another trust bank said.
"The overnight call rate rose a little in the afternoon, as lenders of funds became stubborn," the trader said.
In the morning the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was seen at 0.45 percent, but it may come out higher due to the key rate's rise in the afternoon, the trader said.
On Thursday, the weighted average for the overnight call rate was 0.47 percent.

Thirty billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.51 percent. One- and two-month CDs were tagged with sell quotes of 0.49 percent and 0.50 percent, respectively. All CD rates were unchanged.
